naming: The loader reads the document with YamlDotNet's CamelCaseNamingConvention and refuses any key it does not know.

keys.description: Always mapping: this document fills one OSDU template.
The mapping's name. With version it makes the reference Name@version a delivery flow pins under render.mapping, and the file is mappings/Name@version.yaml.
The mapping's version. It is part of the reference Name@version and of every rendered record's render context, so a new version re-renders the records that use it.
Free text describing what the mapping delivers.
The saved template version the mapping fills. A run refuses to render against any other, and one the catalog does not hold stops the run.
The OSDU kind of the records the mapping renders, authority:source:entityType:major.minor.patch, such as osdu:wks:work-product-component--WellLog:1.4.0.
The saved template version: the 16 hexadecimal characters the Templates page and 'sqlflow template list' show for the kind.
The rows the mapping renders: the source system, the key the delivery key and the OSDU id are derived from, and what identifies a record to a person.
The source system. It enters the delivery key, and so the OSDU id: two mappings that deliver the same rows into the same entity type and partition need different systems or keys.

The columns of the dataset's row that identify a record, in order, each written dataset.<column>. The delivery key, and so the OSDU id, is derived from them; a key column need not be written into the record.
A key column, written dataset.<column>.
Optional display text for the ledger and the GUI, with {dataset.<column>} tokens, cut at 400 characters. It never enters the record.

Optional columns whose values identify the record to a person (a wellbore id, a log id). The ledger indexes every value, so the Records page finds the record by any of them. Search only: never in the record.
An identifying column, written dataset.<column>.
Values the flow supplies under render.parameters, each declared here. dataPartition is always declared, and a flow value for a parameter the mapping does not declare is refused.
One parameter, read in static values as {param.<name>}.
True when the flow has to supply the parameter (or it has a default).
The value used when the flow supplies none. It is mapping content and is not expanded as a reference.
Free text describing the parameter.
The record sets the mapping's search.<name> sources look in on the platform, as each record needs one, rather than capturing them into the cache. One search per kind, each read by an entry.
One search, read by entries as search.<name>.id.
The kind searched: one entity type, at one version or every version, such as osdu:wks:master-data--Wellbore:*.
The saved template whose schema says how the searched kind's properties are indexed, so a findBy line is asked the way the platform answers it.
The kind of the saved template, such as osdu:wks:master-data--Wellbore:1.3.0.
The saved template version: 16 hexadecimal characters.
Free text describing the search.
The entries, at least one: each names a template variable and where its value comes from. A variable without an entry is left out of the record, and no two entries fill the same variable.
One entry: the variable it fills (target) and where the value comes from (source or static), with the lookup, modifiers and condition that apply.
The template variable to fill: osdu. and the property's path in the record, with [] after an array of objects (osdu.data.Curves[].CurveID). A path steps into at most one array.

Where the value comes from: dataset.<column>, dataset.<child>.<column>, dataset.<child> (a repeater), cache.<Type>.id, cache.<Type>.<field>, or search.<name>.id. An entry has source or static, never both.

A fixed value: text, a number, a boolean, a list or an object. {param.name} tokens in its text are replaced with the flow's parameter values. A static entry takes only appliesWhen and description besides.

With a cache or a search source, and required there: which record to read. One line or a list, such as cache.UnitOfMeasure.Code = dataset.unit; the lines are tried in order and the first that finds exactly one record wins.
Changes to the incoming dataset value, applied top to bottom. On a cache or search source they change the value findBy compares; cached values and platform records are never modified.

A modifier: a name (trim, upper, lower, date, number) or one setting (split, replace, equals, date, number) written as a one-key mapping. Only replace takes settings beside it: otherwise, and for a cached table match and field.
Splits the value and keeps one part: split: { separator: ",", part: 1 }. A part the value does not have, or an empty one, gives an empty value.
The text the value is split on. A single space splits on any run of whitespace.
The part to keep, counting from one.

Replaces the trimmed value. Written as a table ({ M: m, NONE: ~ }) it lists incoming values and what each becomes, ~ being no value. Written as cache.<Type> it reads the table from the partition's cache: a dictionary, an ingestion table or OSDU reference data. A value is matched exactly first, then ignoring case when that finds one row.
An incoming value, and what it becomes: text, or ~ for no value, so the entry's required flag decides.
What a value the table does not list becomes: left out, it passes on unchanged; ~ gives no value; any other text replaces it. Written beside replace, never inside its table.
For a table read from the cache: the cached field the incoming value is compared with. It defaults to the table's key; a type of OSDU records has none, so it is named there.

For a table read from the cache: the cached field that replaces the value. It defaults to the one field a lookup table holds beside its key (value, for a dictionary of pairs); a table with several fields, and a type of OSDU records, names it. A row with nothing there gives no value.
Gives true when the trimmed value equals this text, ignoring case, and false otherwise. The entry's last modifier being equals, it must fill a boolean.

Reads the value as a date in this .NET format (dd.MM.yyyy) and writes it in the form the template's format names: a full-date for a date, a UTC date-time otherwise. Without a format (- date) it reads ISO 8601 only.
Reads the value as a number written with these separators: number: { decimal: ",", group: " " }. Without settings (- number) the decimal separator is a point and there is no group separator.
The separator before the decimals: . or ,.
The separator between groups of three digits, when the value is written with one.
When the entry applies to a row: dataset.<column> is <text>, is not <text>, is empty or is not empty (trimmed text, ignoring case). When it does not, the variable is left out for that row.
What an empty value does: true (the default) holds the record, false leaves the variable out.
With a cache source: a last matching attempt with punctuation and spacing folded away on both sides, for names rather than codes.
Free text describing the entry.
Example rows and the exact record each must render to under the pinned template and cache. The preflight gate renders them before every run: the mapping's regression suite.
One fixture: a row, the parameters and search answers it renders with, and the record it must render to.
What the fixture shows.
The render parameters the fixture renders with.
A parameter's value.
The dataset's row: its columns and values.
A column's value.
Child dataset rows, by child dataset name.
The rows of one child dataset.
One child row: its columns and values.
A column's value.
What the platform is assumed to answer to each search the render asks; a fixture never asks it.
One answer the platform is assumed to give: the search, the property and value asked for, and the record found.
The search, by its name under searches.
The property the findBy line compares, such as data.FacilityName.
The value asked for.
The one record found; left out when the platform holds no such record.
The exact record the row renders to, as JSON, compared canonically.
